articles.headline: Bahrain accuses Iran of industrial site strike as tankers are hit in Hormuz
articles.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
articles.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of targeting a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, causing a fire but no casualties, while two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred amid an ongoing maritime conflict and US counterblockade efforts. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated a Qatari delegation visited Tehran for talks, as Tehran maintained its demands for lifting blockades.
articles.description: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

articles.title: Trump says he wants ‘permanent’ deal to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons
articles.description: US President Donald Trump says he wants a permanent agreement to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills two people and injures 60 in Kryvyi Rih
articles.title: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
articles.summary: An assault on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine resulted in multiple casualties after missiles struck residential buildings and medical facilities. Local officials reported that emergency workers were subsequently hit by secondary blasts during rescue operations. The military escalation comes amid ongoing international diplomatic efforts involving United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leaders to negotiate an end to the ongoing armed conflict.
articles.description: Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.

articles.headline: Polish territory struck by suspected Russian missiles and drone
articles.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
articles.summary: Polish officials stated that two missiles and a jet-powered drone landed in southeastern Poland during a heavy Russian bombardment of Ukraine. The incident prompted security concerns among North Atlantic Treaty Organization allies and coincided with ongoing diplomatic efforts involving the United States to negotiate an end to the conflict.
articles.description: Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but bar for triggering NATO's collective defence clause remains high.

articles.headline: Iran Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps downs two United States drones over Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled
articles.summary: Iranian forces intercepted and shot down two United States drones over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The incident occurred on Saturday amid ongoing military tensions and stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. Meanwhile, the United States Treasury imposed new sanctions on four Iranian individuals accused of acting as oil trustees to evade maritime blockades.
articles.description: Iran reiterates conditions for Hormuz reopening as US slaps sanctions on four Iranians it says acted as 'oil trustees'.

articles.headline: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail
articles.title: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail in Pannun murder plot
articles.summary: A U.S. federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on November 20, 2026. The 55-year-old pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire and money laundering charges related to a plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. The verdict was delivered by Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York.
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with his efforts to murder Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York

articles.headline: Russian missile violates Polish airspace during military exercises
articles.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
articles.summary: Poland reported that a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that breached its airspace on Friday during major aerial attacks on Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incursion as a provocation coinciding with Western military exercises. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the grave violations, confirming that alliance jets were scrambled in response to the ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

articles.title: Dashcam captures Russian missile strike on Lviv, Ukraine

articles.headline: Max Verstappen wins the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time
articles.title: Max Verstappen wins the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years
articles.summary: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen secured victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 22, 2026, holding off competitors during a race featuring thirty-five lead changes. Starting from pole position, Verstappen triumphed after early battles with George Russell and late pressure from Lando Norris. Oscar Piastri finished third, while Russell crashed near the end to take ninth place.
articles.description: Verstappen started from the pole position, but was under pressure from the start before pulling away from Norris, the 2025 series champion, on the final lap. Oscar Piastri finished third and current champ Antonelli fourth

articles.headline: Somalia expels Emirati ambassador and recalls envoy from Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE
articles.summary: Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave Mogadishu on November 19, 2026, and recalled its own envoy following the annulment of several bilateral agreements. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused Abu Dhabi of undermining national security and financing regional rivals. The diplomatic rupture stems from escalating tensions over federal authority and regional administrations.
articles.description: Behind Somalia's break with the UAE lies a domestic power struggle with regional leaders close to Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit faces delays as co-hosts release new draft agreement
articles.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at COP31 climate summit
articles.summary: Negotiators at the United Nation COP31 summit in Antalya faced further delays on November 22, 2026, after co-hosts Turkey and Australia released a revised draft agreement. The text omits explicit calls to transition away from fossil fuels, drawing criticism from the European Union. Turkey Environment Minister Murat Kurum expressed hope for a breakthrough despite ongoing disputes over finance and targets.
articles.description: The UN COP31 meeting in Turkey enters a second day of overtime as countries struggle to reach an agreement.

articles.headline: COP31 final draft agreement omits specific mention of fossil fuels
articles.title: COP31: Turkiye's final draft doesn't mention the words ‘fossil fuels’ that cause global warming
articles.summary: Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum released the latest draft agreement for the COP31 summit in Antalya on November 22, 2026, omitting any reference to fossil fuels. The text includes a controversial goal for carbon capture and storage while addressing clean energy consumption targets. Delegates received limited time to review the proposal as negotiations stretched into overtime.
articles.description: COP31 President Murat Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary

articles.headline: United States restricts remote access to advanced AI chips for Chinese firms
articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.summary: The United States Commerce Department introduced new regulations on November 17, 2026, to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI chips via data centres in third-party nations. The rule mandates export licenses for semiconductors sent to countries like Malaysia and Singapore. Beijing condemned the move, accusing Washington of abusing export controls to hinder China's technological development.
articles.description: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge and oil facilities as Putin and Trump meet in Shenzhen
articles.title: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Putin ally declares ‘no one needs Europe’
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-day operation targeting the Kerch Bridge, damaging its road and rail sections, while also striking oil depots and the Rostov-Crimea highway to disrupt Russian supply lines. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on November 19, discussing peace proposals regarding Ukraine and European security architecture.
articles.description: Russia-Europe tensions rise as Ukraine uses its own weapons and communications tech to hit the Kerch Bridge.

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks enter overtime as Turkish officials propose fossil fuel text
articles.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, summit president says
articles.summary: Negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya extended discussions into a second day of overtime after Turkish officials introduced a last-minute compromise addressing fossil fuels. Murat Kurum, the Turkish environment minister and summit president, stated the conference would reconvene to approve the deal following intense consultations between Australia, Turkiye, and nearly 200 delegations.
articles.description: New draft would acknowledge for the first time that global ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠warming is on course to pass 1.5°C.

articles.headline: Russian president compares Shenzhen trilateral summit to 1945 Yalta Conference
articles.title: The Shenzhen trilateral | The unlikely trio
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin drew comparisons between a recent trilateral summit with American and Chinese leaders in Shenzhen and the 1945 Yalta Conference. Speaking to the press on November 19, 2026, Putin suggested that codifying a victory over neo-Nazism would be appropriate, similar to how the historic Crimean summit involving Soviet, American, and British leaders shaped the post-war European political order.
articles.description: Leaders of the U.S., Russia and China agreed to begin talks on nuclear risk reduction but offered no details on institutionalising the dialogue process

articles.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.summary: In a historic ruling, the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya during military clearance operations in Rakhine State in 2017. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate perpetrators, ensure non-repetition, and allow the safe return of displaced persons. The final judgment resulted from a case brought by The Gambia in 2019.
articles.description: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

articles.headline: Displaced Palestinians protest in Gaza as Israeli strikes and home destructions continue
articles.title: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
articles.summary: Hundreds of displaced residents demonstrated near Deir el-Balah to protest against intensifying air strikes and property destructions by Israeli forces beyond the Yellow Line established under a ceasefire. According to local officials, recent attacks have left hundreds of thousands homeless, while continuing military operations and recent strikes have caused numerous casualties across the enclave.
articles.description: Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a 'gradual displacement' policy, a Gaza mayor says.

articles.headline: Thousands march in Lisbon to protest soaring living costs and housing crisis
articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.summary: Thousands of individuals participated in a central Lisbon march on November 21, 2026, organised by trade union federation CGTP to protest against increasing living costs, low wages, and a severe housing crisis. Protesters demanded higher wages and lower prices. Portugal faces high inflation and surging property prices, compounding economic pressures experienced by workers and younger generations across the country.
articles.description: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

articles.headline: Mexican special forces arrest top FBI most-wanted drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores
articles.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
articles.summary: Mexican special forces detained alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa, following a shoot-out involving gunfire and explosives. Meza Flores, leader of the Meza Flores Organisation and on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was flown to Mexico City to face extradition and prosecution. The operation occurred amid increased Mexican efforts to combat cartels under US pressure.
articles.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

articles.summary: Russia launched nearly one hundred missiles and four hundred drones targeting Ukrainian infrastructure, hitting three Dnipro River bridges in Kyiv and killing six individuals. Additional strikes in Lviv claimed two lives at a railway station, while Polish forces investigated a projectile landing near the border. Officials reported widespread injuries, power disruptions, and ongoing air raid sirens across nine regions.
articles.description: Russia launched one of its biggest air attacks yet as it rejected the prospect of security guarantees for Ukraine.

articles.headline: Federal Bureau of Investigation investigates apparent hack of criminal information database
articles.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center database, according to United States media reports citing two briefed sources. The database is utilized by law enforcement agencies to share information regarding warrants and background checks. This development follows recent high-profile cybersecurity incidents and the firing of White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.
articles.description: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

articles.headline: U.S. Commerce Department issues interim rule restricting advanced AI chip exports
articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on November 16, 2026, barring foreign data centers with American AI chips from providing cloud services to businesses in twenty-four countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. China criticized the move as an overreach of national security, while the policy builds on export controls established in 2018.
articles.description: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

articles.headline: Lebanese president demands Israeli withdrawal and condemns Iranian interference
articles.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
articles.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun criticized Iranian meddling and demanded a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon in a speech ahead of the country's independence anniversary. According to authorities, ongoing Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon have killed thousands of people since fighting began. Aoun also pledged to bring all armed groups under state control.
articles.description: Joseph Aoun says 'two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked' mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit deadlocked over fossil fuel reduction references
articles.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
articles.summary: Negotiations at the COP31 United Nations climate summit in Turkey entered a deadlock after a group of nations led by France and Panama opposed a draft agreement omitting references to reducing fossil fuel demand. Disagreements also persist over funding for adaptation, with African nations demanding increased financial support. A new agreement is anticipated as discussions continue among participating international ministers.
articles.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

articles.headline: Bahrain reports industrial facility fire following Iranian aerial attack
articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial facility
articles.summary: Bahrain announced that an Iranian aerial attack struck a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries, according to the Bahrain Defence Force and the Ministry of Interior. Meanwhile, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it targeted United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in response to airspace violations. The incident occurred amid escalating regional conflict involving Gulf Arab states and Iran.
articles.description: Bahrain reports no injuries as Iran's IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.

articles.headline: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot invites Likud party for coalition talks
articles.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming the next Israeli government, invited caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party for coalition talks beginning on Sunday, November 22, 2026. The centrist Yashar party leader stated the meetings reflect a commitment to forming a broad government. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett expressed opposition to joining Netanyahu's bloc.
articles.description: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

articles.title: Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
articles.summary: Iranian officials met with Qatari mediators in Tehran to discuss terms for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Washington must accept conditions including the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the economic blockade before shipping lanes can be restored following the conflict that began on February 28.
articles.description: Iran's foreign minister says reopening the strait is 'not difficult' if the US accepts reasonable conditions.

articles.title: 11 killed in burst of violence in northern Mexico after capture of cartel leader Meza Flores
articles.summary: At least eleven people were killed during clashes in Guasave after Mexican forces captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores. The Defense Cabinet reported that seven alleged gunmen and four soldiers died in the violence. The operation relied on intelligence from the United States administration and led to widespread roadblocks with burning vehicles across the municipality.
articles.description: Flores climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán-Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation

articles.headline: United Nations diplomats agree to discuss autonomous weapons rules over two years
articles.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
articles.summary: Diplomats meeting in Geneva failed to establish binding regulations for autonomous weapons during discussions. According to NPR, the United States, Russia, and Israel obstructed the proceedings. Representatives ultimately agreed to spend two years considering optional guidelines instead of the urgent legally binding framework requested by the International Committee of the Red Cross.
articles.description: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called "killer robots." articles.headline: Russian cargo vessel hit by drone attack in the Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: A cargo ship registered in Russia sustained damage and caught fire following an aerial drone strike while navigating through eastern maritime waters near Finland. Finnish defense forces indicated that Ukraine likely orchestrated the assault, which prompted temporary regional transit restrictions. Local authorities confirmed that the vessel's crew remained onboard to conduct necessary repairs, while regional officials monitored potential security implications stemming from the incident.
articles.description: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.

articles.headline: FBI national criminal database suffers suspected security breach
articles.title: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
articles.summary: United States media reports indicated that the National Crime Information Center experienced a compromise affecting law enforcement agencies nationwide. United States President Donald Trump commented on the situation during a media appearance, suggesting potential investigative insights might emerge from the incident. articles.headline: Iran expresses desire for diplomatic resolution to ongoing conflict
articles.title: Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms
articles.summary: Tehran officials stated a continued commitment to pursuing negotiated agreements following recent military hostilities involving the United States and Israel. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi emphasized the need for substantial guarantees from Washington during ongoing discussions facilitated by regional mediators. Meanwhile, United States President Donald Trump asserted that existing proposals from Tehran failed to meet American standards, as diplomatic and military tensions persist across the region.
articles.description: Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside Iran, he says, adding that ‘a fair solution’ could be reached; U.S. denies Iran fired at an F-16

articles.headline: Yemeni Houthis launch ballistic missiles toward Riyadh following coalition operation
articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.summary: Armed factions based in Yemen executed retaliatory aerial attacks targeting the Saudi Arabian capital following a military operation conducted by a coalition supporting the recognized government. Coalition representatives reported intercepting multiple incoming projectiles, although structural damage occurred near the border region. The cross-border escalations follow months of renewed fighting in the civil conflict, raising international concern regarding regional stability and civilian safety.
articles.description: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20

articles.headline: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
articles.summary: An Israeli military attack killed three Palestinians inside a vehicle carrying food and papers for the World Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on November 21, 2026. Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses confirmed the strike, while the charity stated the vehicle was unaffiliated. The Israeli military reported targeting militants in the area without explaining the vehicle strike. The incident occurred amid ongoing violence following an October 2025 United States-backed ceasefire.
articles.description: Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack

articles.headline: Cargo ship struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad hit by drones, Finland tightens security
articles.summary: A cargo ship traveling to Russia's Kaliningrad exclave was struck by drones in international waters within the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026, according to Russian and Finnish authorities. The vessel caught fire and drifted into Finnish territorial waters. Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko reported two drone strikes near Gogland island. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo warned that the war was spreading to neighboring regions as local security measures were tightened.
articles.description: Finland's Defence Ministry said the military had reintroduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution to protect civilians and enable authorities ​to operate if drones needed ‌to be intercepted.

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills two in Kryvyi Rih
articles.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills 2
articles.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, killed two people and wounded sixty others on November 21, 2026. City administration head Oleksandr Vilkul reported that subsequent rockets struck emergency crews responding to the initial explosions. The assault damaged numerous residential buildings, a hospital, schools, and vehicles. The escalation coincided with increased tensions surrounding international mediation efforts and separate military incidents involving Poland and a Russian cargo ship.
articles.description: The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington; It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland

articles.headline: Delhi court frames charges against fourteen in NEET paper leak
articles.title: NEET paper leak case: Delhi court frames charges against 14 accused
articles.summary: A Delhi court formally framed charges against fourteen individuals on November 21, 2026, regarding the NEET-UG paper leak case, initiating trial proceedings for November 25, 2026. Special Judge Ajay Gupta instituted the charges after the accused pleaded not guilty to offences including cheating and criminal breach of trust. Public servants engaged by the National Testing Agency and eleven private individuals face prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Prevention of Corruption Act.
articles.description: Special Judge Ajay Gupta framed the charges after noting the accused pleaded ‘not guilty’, with the trial set to begin on a day-to-day basis from November 25

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold trilateral summit in Shenzhen
articles.title: U.S., China, Russia hold historic summit in Shenzhen
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, for their first trilateral summit. The three leaders discussed strategic stability, international security, and nuclear risk reduction. According to Mr. Xi, major powers must take legitimate security concerns seriously and resolve differences through dialogue, while emphasizing cooperation to confront global security challenges.
articles.description: The three heads of state — Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump — had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security

articles.headline: Anthropic shares soar on Nasdaq debut following record initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic saw its shares surge thirty four percent during its Nasdaq debut on November nineteen, twenty twenty six, after raising a record eighty one billion dollars. Chief executive Dario Amodei spoke in New York about the company's financial position, while protesters gathered outside and analysts debated market valuations and computing costs.
articles.description: The shares ended the session at around $97, up from an IPO price of $83, after opening at $111.50 and briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion

articles.headline: Anthropic prices initial public offering at eighty three dollars per share
articles.title: Anthropic raises $81 billion in IPO amid AI market volatility
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence chatbot Claude developer Anthropic priced its initial public offering at eighty three dollars per share on November eighteen, twenty twenty six, aiming to raise approximately eighty one billion dollars. The listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market occurs amid broader market volatility and investor scrutiny regarding artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.
articles.description: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

articles.headline: India emerges as crucial swing vote ahead of IMO shipping decarbonisation meeting
articles.title: India a swing vote at IMO meeting on shipping decarbonisation
articles.summary: India is considered a key swing state ahead of the International Maritime Organization meeting scheduled in London from November 23, 2026, with a vote expected on December 4. Stakeholders seek India's intervention on net zero goals. India has not finalised its stance, which will likely align with climate justice principles and national interests as a fossil fuel importer.

articles.headline: Tankers struck by projectiles in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
articles.summary: British maritime authorities reported two separate incidents where oil tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles near Oman in the Strait of Hormuz on November 21, 2026. Meanwhile, Iran's navy claimed responsibility for an oil tanker fire after a vessel allegedly struck a naval mine while ignoring warnings. The region has experienced rising maritime incidents as Tehran attempts to enforce strict navigation controls through the critical waterway.
articles.description: British maritime agency reports two incidents near Oman, while Iran says a tanker caught fire due to naval mine.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Chief Justice favors AI regulation over total ban in legal education

articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant stated during a legal education conference in New Delhi that establishing clear regulatory rules for artificial intelligence is preferable to an outright ban. He emphasized that law schools must improve assessment methods to ensure authentic student knowledge. Other officials discussed the global challenges of technology and the necessity of adapting legal training standards.
articles.description: Generative artificial intelligence had unsettled the assumption that an answer sheet reflects the knowledge of a student, Justice Surya Kant said

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskiy dismisses trilateral summit as unsuccessful for Russian leadership

articles.description: The Ukrainian President said Vladimir Putin had failed to recreate the Yalta conference, and that it is not clear to Kyiv whether it will be able to join NATO

Border guards confirmed that the vessel caught fire and drifted toward Finnish territory following the incident. Prime Minister Petteri Orpo noted that the regional conflict is expanding, while Finnish authorities informed NATO and established temporary maritime restrictions.
articles.description: The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor”

articles.headline: Ukrainian president defends bridge strikes during British official visit
articles.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy defended attacks on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea as a fair response to Russian strikes. Speaking in Kyiv alongside United Kingdom Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, Zelenskyy asserted that the military route serves as a vital logistics supply line for Russian forces.
articles.description: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Iranian foreign minister states allies oppose nuclear doctrine change
articles.title: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that China and Russia oppose any modification to Tehran's nuclear doctrine amid domestic political debate. While hardliners advocate for a shift toward developing a deterrent, officials continue to reference a historical religious decree prohibiting weapons of mass destruction.
articles.description: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities

articles.headline: European leaders state readiness for peace talks with Russia
articles.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
articles.summary: European leaders declared their readiness for negotiations with Russia to end the war in Ukraine during a summit in Berlin. US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner stated that Russia was comfortable with Ukraine receiving security guarantees, though Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed skepticism and reported attacks on Kyiv and the Crimean Bridge, underscoring ongoing conflict alongside diplomatic discussions.
articles.description: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.

articles.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims proof of Riemann hypothesis with artificial intelligence
articles.title: Riemann hypothesis: Has the world’s most famous maths problem been cracked?
articles.summary: Levent Alpoge, a researcher at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, announced a claimed proof for the generalized Riemann hypothesis using the Claude model. Released in the Lean programming language on November 20, 2026, the 17-million-line argument is currently undergoing verification by independent mathematicians worldwide. If confirmed, the achievement would resolve a major mathematical problem that has remained unsolved for 167 years.
articles.description: Mathematicians say the claimed proof, made with Claude, could be historic, but it may take weeks to understand it.

articles.headline: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Crew evacuated amid battle to put out fire on Russian ship hit by drones
articles.summary: Emergency operations are under way in the Gulf of Finland after a Russian cargo vessel named Sparta II was struck by two drones near Russia's maritime border. Finnish authorities reported that the damaged ship drifted into Finnish territorial waters west of Gogland Island. Officials confirmed the crew has not abandoned the vessel and no environmental damage has occurred yet, while security restrictions were implemented in the region.
articles.description: Finnish authorities say two drones attack cargo ship that has links to Russia's armed forces.

articles.headline: European Union proposes digital company tax for budget funding
articles.title: European Union proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
articles.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa presented a revised budget proposal that introduces a tax on major digital companies to help bridge funding divisions among member states. The draft targets firms with significant European Union and global turnovers, potentially drawing opposition from the United States administration.
articles.description: European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros a plan initially put forward by the European Commission

articles.headline: Elderly displaced Sudanese face severe hardships in camps
articles.title: Sudan’s elderly face hardship and heartbreak in a life of displacement
articles.summary: Displaced senior citizens in Sudan are struggling with extreme poverty, hunger, and family separation amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. Hamad Mohammed Adam, seventy, is among thousands residing at the al-Moulih camp in western Omdurman after fleeing violence in northern Kordofan. Officials emphasize the urgent need for specialized humanitarian assistance and social protection services for vulnerable older populations.
articles.description: Sudan's displaced elderly often have to support grandchildren or fend for themselves.

articles.headline: Israeli attacks in Gaza kill at least four Palestinians
articles.title: Israeli strike on vehicle distributing food aid in Gaza kills three
articles.summary: Israeli military actions across Gaza have killed at least four Palestinians despite an existing ceasefire agreement. Three individuals died when an aid delivery van was struck by a drone in the Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City, while another man was shot dead in Halawa. Meanwhile, severe winter weather continues to exacerbate the humanitarian crisis, as restrictions prevent more than one hundred thousand tents from entering the enclave.
articles.description: Separately, Palestinian man is shot dead by Israeli forces in Jabalia and three people injured in attack in Khan Younis.

articles.headline: Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel boss in military raid
articles.title: Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel boss in military raid
articles.description: Mexico’s military captured FBI-wanted cartel leader ‘El Chapo Isidro’ in Guasave, Sinaloa.

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic achieves $1.76 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence enterprise Anthropic reached a valuation of approximately $1.76 trillion following its public stock market debut on the Nasdaq exchange on Thursday. Shares opened at $111.50 before closing at $97, outperforming its allocation price of $83. The milestone occurred amid broader tech sector declines, with executives highlighting safety considerations and upcoming regulatory scrutiny.
articles.description: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.

articles.headline: United States and Iran negotiations stall over uranium enrichment dispute
articles.title: Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports
articles.summary: Diplomatic negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile. Mediators from Qatar and Pakistan have warned of potential renewed military escalation in West Asia. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran would not accept an agreement that compromised its national interests or national security.
articles.description: The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme

articles.headline: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate Ukrainian-American rapper
articles.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of planning to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, also known as Kyivstoner, at a Copenhagen concert. Security forces stopped three suspects on 25 September, leading to two attempted murder charges. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attache following the incident, while the Russian embassy rejected the allegations.
articles.description: The Russian embassy in Denmark has denied the allegation, which has led to Russia's defence attaché being expelled.

articles.headline: United Nations conference nations agree to elaborate rules on killer robots by 2028
articles.title: Nations agree to ‘elaborate’ on rules for AI-run ‘killer robots’ by 2028
articles.summary: Delegates from one hundred twenty-eight countries at a United Nations conference in Geneva agreed to elaborate on a possible accord regulating lethal autonomous weapons by 2028. The decision followed a push by nearly one hundred nations for legally binding rules, despite opposition from key arms producers including the United States, Russia, and Israel. Advocacy groups criticized the mandate as watered down and lacking urgency.
articles.description: Members of the UN's Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons fail to agree on swift adoption of legally binding rules.

articles.headline: Kremlin embraces US proposal to discuss post-war European security
articles.title: Russia dusts off its pre-war demands as the U.S. raises discussing European security at Ukraine talks
articles.summary: Following five years of conflict in Ukraine, the Kremlin has welcomed a United States offer to discuss post-war European security. During discussions with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on November 12, 2026, Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed demands first raised in 2021 regarding NATO expansion and military deployments. European leaders and Ukraine have expressed concern over potential negotiations conducted without Kyiv's direct participation.
articles.description: The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by Donald Trump’s envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow’s hands and weaken NATO

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel launches ground offensive in Gaza
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel launches ground offensive in Gaza
articles.description: Israel launches its first major ground offensive in central Gaza, pushing beyond the ‘Yellow Line’ it controls

articles.headline: Illicit alcohol kills eleven people and poisons one hundred eighty in Manipur state
articles.title: Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in northeast India’s Manipur state
articles.summary: At least eleven people died and more than one hundred eighty individuals were hospitalized after consuming toxic illicit alcohol in northeast India's Manipur state. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh confirmed the fatalities and hospitalizations in a statement issued on Friday. Authorities advised residents in Sugnu town to seek medical evaluation following the consumption of unregulated liquor.
articles.description: Manipur's chief minister orders a probe into the incident, saying those responsible will be arrested and punished.

articles.headline: Trump highlights trade deals and low interest rates during Washington briefing
articles.title: ‘Look at India, they have low interest rates’: Trump says U.S. could achieve 14–15% economic growth
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced new trade agreements with Thailand and the Philippines while speaking at the White House on November 20, 2026. He noted that lower interest rates could help the United States achieve significantly higher economic growth. Additionally, he discussed cooperation measures agreed upon during a recent meeting with leaders of the Quad alliance.
articles.description: “In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Donald Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington

articles.headline: Zelensky labels Putin a killer following Trump remarks
articles.title: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Vladimir Putin as an enemy and a killer during a CNN interview after Donald Trump referred to the Russian leader as a friend following trilateral talks in China. The exchange coincided with massive Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine that caused civilian casualties, alongside a reported airspace violation in Poland.
articles.description: Earlier this week, Trump greeted Putin ahead of a meeting in China and said the pair have a "great relationship".

articles.headline: United Nations court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority population
articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during a twenty seventeen military crackdown. Court president Yuji Iwasawa cited evidence of intent to destroy the population, marking the first time an international court has found a sovereign state guilty of genocide.
articles.description: The unprecedented International Court of Justice verdict concerns a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands.

articles.headline: Supreme Court halts relocation of Central Secretariat Library books
articles.title: SC pulls up Centre over relocation of heritage library, halts shifting of books
articles.summary: The Supreme Court criticised the Centre for an ad hoc approach and ordered a halt to shifting books from the Central Secretariat Library in Shastri Bhawan until November 20, 2026. A Bench headed by Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva intervened following directives to vacate the premises for the Central Vista project. The Centre plans to relocate the library to Kartavya Bhawan-4 by December 2028.
articles.description: Bench to examine government’s proposal to permanently relocate the library to the under-construction Kartavya Bhawan-4 in central Delhi as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project

articles.headline: European leaders gather in Berlin to affirm support for Ukraine
articles.title: Kushner says Russia ‘comfortable’ with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine
articles.summary: European leaders gathered in Berlin for talks on Ukraine following a summit in Shenzhen between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stressed Europe must be involved in peace negotiations. French President Emmanuel Macron urged allies to increase military aid and reconsider NATO accession for Ukraine, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for sustained international pressure on Russia.
articles.description: European leaders meet in Berlin after Trump summit with Putin and Xi. Putin vows to retaliate for Kerch Bridge strikes.

articles.headline: Emergency crews in Ukraine hit by a double-tap strike
articles.title: Emergency crews in Ukraine hit by a double-tap strike
articles.description: Video shows emergency crews in Ukraine approaching the scene of a Russian strike, before another strike hits.

articles.headline: CCMB researchers identify genes that stimulate nerve regeneration
articles.title: CCMB team identifies genes that spur nerve repair, raise possibility of paralysis treatment
articles.summary: Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad have identified two developmental genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, that restore the ability of damaged nerve cells to regenerate. Published in The EMBO Journal on November 20, 2026, the preclinical study demonstrated that restoring these genes in mice led to severed nerve fibres regrowing across spinal cords and improved mobility, offering a potential framework for treating paralysis.

articles.headline: FBI investigates suspected breach of criminal information database
articles.title: FBI, U.S. Agriculture Department breached by hackers, reports say
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is probing an apparent compromise of the National Crime Information Center database used by law enforcement agencies, according to reports on Friday, November 20, 2026. This potential incident follows a recent string of high-profile cyber disruptions, including a September breach affecting an FBI jobs website by the extortion group ShinyHunters.
articles.description: The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages like the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration

articles.headline: Pakistan climate minister arrives in Delhi for SCO forum
articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.summary: Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik, arrived in Delhi on November 20, 2026, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Representing the current CHS chair nation, Mr. Malik joined the cultural meeting inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the historic Purana Quila.
articles.description: Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun

articles.headline: Spurious liquor consumption kills eleven people in Manipur
articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur
articles.summary: At least eleven people have died and over three hundred have been hospitalized following the consumption of suspected toxic alcohol in Manipur's Chandel district. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited affected patients at hospitals in Imphal on Friday, November 20, 2026. Authorities deployed medical teams to the area and announced an official inquiry into the incident involving methanol poisoning.
articles.description: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications

articles.headline: China’s Xi urges US and Russia to join forces to safeguard world peace
articles.title: China’s Xi urges US and Russia to join forces to safeguard world peace
articles.description: Chinese President Xi urged US President Trump and Russian President Putin to work with China to safeguard world peace.

articles.headline: Leaders issue joint peace declaration after historic trilateral talks in China
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping issued a joint peace declaration on Thursday following their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China. The ninety minute meeting addressed nuclear proliferation, petroleum production, and the war in Ukraine, drawing mixed reactions from international observers and lawmakers.
articles.description: While the presidents have previously met for one-on-one meetings, this is their first trilateral discussion.

articles.headline: Human and AI solutions for Riemann hypothesis emerge on same day
articles.title: ‘All human, no AI’ Riemann hypothesis proof out on same day as Claude’s claim
articles.summary: On November 20, two proposed solutions to the Riemann hypothesis emerged within hours of each other, highlighting a debate over artificial intelligence in mathematics. Levent Alpöge at Anthropic announced a proof with the AI model Claude, while American Mathematical Society president Ravi Vakil shared a human-only manuscript by Alessandro Maria Masullo from Stanford University.
articles.description: ‘We are still here. We are very much alive. We are not going anywhere,’ mathematician Alessandro Masullo wrote in his paper detailing his efforts to crack mathematics’s greatest unsolved problem

articles.headline: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
articles.summary: Israeli forces initiated a targeted ground operation in the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, advancing tanks near the Nuseirat refugee camp and closing a section of the Salah al-Din road. According to the Israeli military, the objective was to dismantle a tunnel. Hamas condemned the incursion as a ceasefire violation, while Gaza's Civil Defence agency reported three deaths from separate drone strikes.
articles.description: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.

articles.headline: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq following massive public offering debut
articles.title: Anthropic starts trading in the US after blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic launched trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after executing a historic public offering. The company priced ninety eight crore shares at eighty three dollars each, achieving a valuation of two trillion dollars while facing scrutiny over potential technological risks and net losses.
articles.description: Anthropic’s IPO surpasses SpaceX, marking the largest initial public offering in US history at $81bn.

articles.headline: India awaits concrete details following trilateral summit between US, Russia, and China
articles.title: India ‘takes note’ of Trump-Xi-Putin summit, awaits more details
articles.summary: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated on November 20, 2026, that India has taken note of the recent trilateral summit held in Shenzhen between American, Russian, and Chinese leaders. While awaiting further details of the meeting outcomes, officials emphasized India's separate engagements through the Quad framework following criticism from domestic opposition politicians.
articles.description: Opposition questions why India not present at 'G-3' global power summit in Shenzhen; Ministry cites ‘concrete outcomes’ of Quad Summit held earlier in the week

articles.headline: Anthropic goes public on Nasdaq with ticker ANT
articles.title: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT at $111.50 per share, following its initial $83 per share price. CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company will pace its AI training to ensure safety and maintain human control. The firm previously reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of the year alongside $16.3 billion in revenue.
articles.description: Anthropic has officially gone public. It began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" at $111.50 per share, up from its initial $83 per share price that put company's value at around $1.5 trillion. The listing comes nearly a month after Anthropic revealed its plans to go public. In its lengthy S-1 filing, […]

articles.headline: Los Angeles jury convicts man of starting deadly wildfire
articles.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
articles.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht was found guilty of two federal charges for starting the January wildfire in Pacific Palisades and Malibu that killed twelve people and destroyed thousands of structures. The conviction follows a previous mistrial. Prosecutors presented geolocation and camera evidence showing he targeted the area out of anger. Sentencing is scheduled for March seventeen.
articles.description: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted three ballistic missiles fired by Houthi rebels toward Riyadh following multiple emergency alerts in the capital. The attack follows previous strikes on infrastructure. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki stated that retaliatory special operations targeted smuggling capabilities at the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, prompting concern from the United Nations regarding humanitarian supply routes.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia issues emergency alerts in Riyadh for third night in row, as the Houthis threaten ports and power station.

articles.headline: Anthropic researcher claims solution to Riemann hypothesis using artificial intelligence
articles.title: AI cracks math’s most famous problem. Have mathematicians lost a guiding light?
articles.summary: Levent Alpöge of artificial intelligence firm Anthropic announced on November 20, 2026, that he generated a proof for the Riemann hypothesis using the Claude model. The researcher published 1.7 crore lines of code without a traditional paper. Independent mathematicians and proof systems verified the code passes checks, though the Clay Mathematics Institute bounty remains pending for the unsolved mathematical problem.
articles.description: Levent Alpöge of Anthropic has announced that he and the company’s AI model Claude have found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers. Mathematicians have spent more than 160 years trying to prove it

articles.headline: World Court finds Myanmar forces killed thousands of Rohingya
articles.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya, says top UN court
articles.summary: Judges at the International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday, November 19, 2026, that Myanmar security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians and committed widespread sexual violence. According to court president Yuji Iwasawa, evidence supports the estimate of 10,000 violent deaths during 2017 clearance operations, as well as attacks on people fleeing toward Bangladesh. The UN tribunal has not yet ruled on whether genocide occurred.
articles.description: The ruling by the top UN court was the first time in its 80-year history that ICJ judges have determined that a state committed genocide, and is likely to be seen as justice for Rohingya victims of Myanmar’s brutal 2017 crackdown

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three ballistic missiles targeted at Riyadh
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says downed 3 Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh
articles.summary: Air defences intercepted three ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh on November 21, 2026, according to the Saudi-led coalition. Authorities briefly issued an alert for a hostile aerial threat before civil defence declared the danger had passed. Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes, which followed coalition attacks on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida on November 20, 2026.
articles.description: Yemen's Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh

articles.headline: Anthropic faces governance scrutiny following record public offering
articles.title: With the biggest IPO of all time, Anthropic’s ‘good guy’ reputation is on the line
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence lab Anthropic completed a record initial public offering raising $81.3 billion, though legal experts and industry watchdogs questioned the oversight power of its Long-Term Benefit Trust. Critics noted that the structure, designed to protect safety missions, grants founders and trustees complex voting controls while leaving actual artificial intelligence expertise among trustees open to debate.
articles.description: Today is a new beginning for Anthropic: a years-in-the-making IPO that beat out SpaceX for most valuable of all time, having raised $81.3 billion and set an important precedent for the other public AI lab debuts to come. But it's not simply a financial milestone. Anthropic was founded on the idea that it prioritized safety […]

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls for Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.title: Trump calls for Nvidia to reinstate ‘brilliant’ Jensen Huang
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he would support Jensen Huang returning as chief executive officer of Nvidia following his resignation on November 12 over a scandal involving affairs and a suspected Chinese spy. Despite Trump backing Huang and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, Nvidia board chairperson Harvey Jones confirmed the directors unanimously rejected a reinstatement.
articles.description: US president calls tech giant to give former CEO 'a second chance' and urges him to 'make a big apology'.

articles.title: COP31 deal stalls as nations struggle to agree on climate plan
