articles.summary: Arunima Mandal moved to Keralam from Jharkhand to join her father, who sought a better education for his children. A private aided school initially refused her admission before accepting her on the condition that she repeat Class nine. Balancing household chores and isolated by her circumstances, she navigates the challenges of adjusting to her new academic environment.
articles.description: Migrant children confront admission barriers, language shocks, and social stigma despite State-led schemes in Keralam. Initiatives such as Project Roshni aim to integrate migrant students even without full documents, but many face hunger, isolation, and cultural distances that extend beyond language

articles.headline: Young Germans protest military registration and conscription plans
articles.title: ‘We don’t want our future decided by the military’: Young Germans protest
articles.summary: High school student Phil Werring received a compulsory military registration letter from the Bundeswehr in Berlin, facing fines for non-compliance. Conscription returned under the Military Service Modernisation Act passed in January, raising army expansion targets. Thousands of students planned nationwide protests organized by Gen Z Regelt on Friday, voicing anger over militarization and deteriorating school facilities.
articles.description: Ahead of Friday's nationwide rallies, German teenagers explain why they are resisting conscription.

articles.headline: Experts analyze potential global economic impacts of artificial intelligence
articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.summary: Researchers are examining the potential economic impacts of artificial intelligence, drawing comparisons to historical industrial inventions like the steam engine. A primary focus of this analysis is the anticipated increase in labour productivity. Economists evaluate this through the ratio of economic output to workers employed, which can shift via output growth or employment changes.
articles.description: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

articles.headline: US maritime agency warned Iran blockade inflated shipping costs
articles.title: US maritime agency warned Iran blockade was adding to rising Gulf premiums
articles.summary: An internal United States Maritime Administration memo revealed concerns that Washington's blockade of Iran increased commercial shipping risks and insurance premiums. Released through a Freedom of Information Act request, the document followed Central Command attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. War-risk insurance costs surged drastically amid mounting regional conflicts that have disrupted global supply chains since February.
articles.description: US Maritime Administration acknowledged naval blockade's impact on insurance premiums and cargo capacity, memo shows.

articles.headline: Spacecraft BepiColombo approaches final orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
articles.title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage
articles.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft, a joint mission by the European Space Agency and the Japanese Space Agency launched in 2018 from French Guiana, is preparing to enter Mercury's orbit after travelling nearly six billion miles. The mission aims to study the planet's extreme temperatures, ice in craters, and mysterious hollows. Once arrived, the two onboard spacecraft will separate to examine the harsh and little-explored inner Solar System planet closely.
articles.description: The mission is set to give us our best ever view of Mercury - the closest planet to the Sun.

articles.headline: Militant killed and others apprehended during search operations in Manipur
articles.title: Militant killed in encounter with security forces in Manipur
articles.summary: Security forces killed one militant and apprehended several others belonging to a banned faction during a search operation in the Yurembam area of Imphal West district on November 20, 2026, according to officials. The region has experienced ongoing ethnic conflict between Meitei and Kuki communities since May 2023, resulting in hundreds of fatalities, missing persons, and widespread displacement across local districts.
articles.description: "During the gunfight, a militant belonging to a faction of the proscribed Kangleipak Communist Party was killed," says official

articles.headline: European Union urges developing nations to deploy existing climate funds rather than increase targets
articles.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
articles.summary: Vulnerable African nations like Uganda and Malawi face severe droughts and floods but struggle to secure funding because they have not submitted National Adaptation Plans. At the COP31 summit in Turkey, the African Group of Negotiators pushed to triple adaptation finance, but European Union officials argued the priority must be deploying already committed funds effectively. Developing countries globally require billions annually, yet current support falls significantly short of these rising climate needs.
articles.description: African countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey are demanding more funding from developed nations to help them cope with climate change.

articles.headline: Contaminated petrol damages vehicles and deepens financial struggles in Yemen
articles.title: Contaminated petrol leaves Yemeni drivers struggling to make ends meet
articles.summary: Drivers in Sanaa face mounting vehicle repairs and rising fuel prices due to contaminated petrol circulating through local markets. While the Sanaa-based Yemen Petroleum Company attributed the issue to damaged storage facilities from airstrikes, critics and analysts cite import restrictions forcing reliance on substandard fuel. The crisis exacerbates economic hardships amid a decade-long conflict.
articles.description: Drivers in Houthi-controlled areas face rising fuel prices and costly repairs as contaminated petrol damages their cars.

articles.headline: Boston University researchers develop non-verbal video game to study perception in autistic adolescents
articles.title: How do autistic people parse information? A video game can help say
articles.summary: Investigators at Boston University adapted a rodent sensory test into an online video game to assess perception among autistic adolescents without requiring verbal communication. Published on November 19, 2026, the remote tool bypasses language barriers and regional translation needs, potentially expanding clinical research access for participants residing outside major metropolitan specialist centres.
articles.description: Researchers have developed a non-verbal online game that adolescents across the autism spectrum can learn and play; it holds special promise for India by bypassing the need to translate complex clinical instructions into regional languages and allowing clinicians to reach autistic individuals far beyond the major metros

articles.headline: Gem and jewellery council urges vigilance over gold scam
articles.title: Jewellers’ body GJC calls for vigilance as an alleged ‘gold scam’ surfaces
articles.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council has advised industry members and buyers to maintain caution without panicking following reports that Rhenium and Iridium-based alloys are being used to fraudulently increase gold weight. Council Chairman Rajesh Rokde stated that the Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter seriously, while urging jewellers to strengthen quality checks and consumers to verify hallmark details using the official BIS Care App.
articles.description: This comes amid recent media reports regarding certain materials, commonly referred to as Rhenium and Iridium-based alloys, allegedly being used by scamsters to increase the weight of gold without a proportional increase in purity

articles.headline: Security officer pushing minister in Bihar sparks political controversy
articles.title: Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant sparks row
articles.summary: A political dispute emerged in Bihar on Thursday following a viral video from Vaishali district showing a security officer purportedly pushing State Health Minister Nishant Kumar. The incident occurred during an inspection for an upcoming prime ministerial visit. While the opposition blamed the ruling National Democratic Alliance, the Special Security Group attributed the occurrence to human error.
articles.description: Alliance partner Janata Dal (United) objected strongly, saying the Assembly mandate was in Nitish Kumar’s name. The party demanded action, calling it an insult to Nishant and all its workers

articles.headline: Government extends validity of pollution certificates for newer vehicles
articles.title: Why has the Centre extended PUCC validity to three years for newer vehicles?
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has modified regulations surrounding Pollution Under Control Certificates by connecting mandatory emission testing frequency directly to vehicle age and emission standards. Under the revised norms, specific newer Bharat Stage VI vehicles are granted a certificate validity of up to three years, thereby reducing the regular frequency of required vehicle pollution checks across the country.
articles.description: Amendments to sub-rule (7) of Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, were notified on November 13, 2026, and came into effect from the date of notification

articles.headline: Justice Yashwant Varma argues removal proceedings are infructuous after resignation
articles.title: Removal proceedings against me infructuous after resignation: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha Secretariat
articles.summary: Justice Yashwant Varma stated in a September 10 letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh that his removal proceedings became infructuous following his resignation. Responding to an inquiry committee report that found three corruption-related charges against him proven, Mr. Varma maintained his innocence and asserted that his resignation does not admit any allegations.
articles.description: In a letter circulated among MPs on November 19, Justice Varma stated that the proceedings directed toward his removal did not survive his resignation

articles.headline: Canada’s beloved Tim Hortons brews ire over ‘excessive’ Israeli data deal
articles.title: Canada’s beloved Tim Hortons brews ire over ‘excessive’ Israeli data deal
articles.description: Advocates raised concerns about the Tim Horton’s app and consumer privacy and data-sharing.

articles.headline: FlightGlobal reduces active Rafale count in Indian Air Force inventory
articles.title: IAF’s ‘active Rafale count cut to 32’ by FlightGlobal; Defence Ministry disputes claim
articles.summary: British aviation publication FlightGlobal lowered the number of active Rafale fighter jets in the Indian Air Force inventory from 35 to 32 in its World Air Forces directory. Ministry of Defence officials disputed the assessment, stating the data did not originate from the Indian military. India previously procured 36 Rafale fighters from France and recently issued a tender seeking support for the entire fleet.
articles.description: 36 Rafale fighters were purchased from France; FlightGlobal in late 2025 listed 35 aircraft as active, while the latest edition has reduced the number to 32

articles.headline: Viswanathan Anand advises D. Gukesh to enjoy chess before world title defence
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Worry less, enjoy chess more, Anand’s message to Gukesh
articles.summary: Former world chess champion Viswanathan Anand advised Indian player D. Gukesh to relax and enjoy the game ahead of his title defence against Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. Gukesh experienced a dip in form and ranking following a series of disappointing tournament results. Anand also noted that compatriot R. Vaishali will gain confidence from her recent performances ahead of her upcoming championship match.
articles.description: At 20, Gukesh and Sindarov are the youngest participants in a world championship match in chess history

articles.headline: EU Copernicus reports high carbon emissions from Indonesian fires in 2026
articles.title: Indonesian fire emissions third highest on record this year, says EU’s Copernicus
articles.summary: Wildfires in Indonesia generated nearly 200 million metric tonnes of carbon emissions by November 15, 2026, according to the European Union Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service. The figure represents the third-highest annual volume on record, driven by dry El Niño conditions and land clearing. The fires damaged an estimated 8.9 million hectares of land across the Southeast Asian archipelago during the season.
articles.description: This year’s fires in Indonesia produced nearly 200 million metric tonnes of carbon emissions ​by November 15, the European Union’s climate monitoring service ‌said

articles.headline: Colombian citizens protest tax reforms amid debates on US military cooperation
articles.title: Thousands protest Colombia’s tax plans amid row over US military role
articles.summary: Thousands of Colombians protested in Bogota and other cities against proposed tax reforms and rising living costs under President Abelardo de la Espriella. Demonstrators opposed plans to lower the income tax threshold and increase healthcare contributions. Meanwhile, the government denied rejecting a proposal for joint military operations with the United States following discussions with United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
articles.description: Trade unions, students and opposition groups demonstrated in Bogota and other major cities on Thursday.

articles.headline: Brazilian president visits ailing Amazon leader Raoni as government recognizes ancestral land
articles.title: Lula visits ailing Chief Raoni as Brazil recognises Indigenous land
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traveled to Peixoto de Azevedo to meet the ninety-four-year-old Indigenous defender who is receiving palliative care. During the visit, the Ministry of Justice declared the Kapot Nhinore Indigenous Territory as permanent possession for the Mebengokre and Yudja peoples. The newly recognized region covers approximately three hundred sixty-two thousand hectares and faces opposition from rural producers.
articles.description: Lula honours Raoni in Mato Grosso, celebrating his legacy and advancing protection for Kayapo and Yudja ancestral lands.

articles.headline: Srikakulam records heavy rainfall as Cyclonic Storm Akvan approaches
articles.title: Very heavy rain lashes Srikakulam as Akvan moves closer to coast
articles.summary: Sixteen weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded over 100 millimetres of rainfall between November 19 and 20, 2026, as Cyclonic Storm Akvan approached the North Andhra-South Odisha coast. The India Meteorological Department reported that Ichchapuram mandal received 153.25 millimetres. Gale winds reached 100 kilometres per hour near the center as the landfall process began near Gopalpur.
articles.description: The major rainfall activity has been concentrated in the district of Srikakulam alone, while a few stations in Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, have recorded light showers

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for government employees
articles.title: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for Govt employees after 25 years
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet approved scrapping the twenty-five-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job applicants, citing declining fertility rates. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the decision on November 18, 2026, at a meeting in Mandsaur district. Officials stated the rule caused difficulties and that ongoing disciplinary proceedings regarding child counts will terminate immediately, aligning with broader demographic debates on falling birth rates.
articles.description: The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise

articles.headline: Law firm Kirkland and Ellis gave millions in free services
articles.title: Democrats say law firm gave $11.8m in free services to Trump administration
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers in the United States stated that an investigation revealed law firm Kirkland and Ellis provided at least 11.8 million dollars in free legal work to President Donald Trump's administration. Representative Jamie Raskin and Senators Richard Blumenthal and Adam Schiff released the findings on November 20, 2026, calling the sum evidence of official coercion. The firm previously entered settlements with the administration following employment practice investigations.
articles.description: Three top Democrats called Trump's dealings with law firms a case of 'official coercion' and pledged investigations.

articles.headline: Severe fuel shortages cause chaos and violence in Malawi
articles.title: ‘Completely messed up everything’: Malawi’s fuel crisis causes chaos
articles.summary: Persistent fuel shortages across Malawi have sparked violence and long queues at filling stations as motorists struggle to secure dwindling supplies. Motorists spend hours waiting for deliveries, while illegal black market sales flourish despite high prices and safety risks. The Human Rights Defenders Coalition planned nationwide demonstrations on November 17, 2026, demanding the energy minister's resignation over the crisis before police postponed the protests due to security constraints.
articles.description: Motorists and businesses struggle as shortages disrupt daily life.

articles.headline: Justice Nagarathna says high offices do not ensure equality
articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that women holding high public office does not prove that societal equality has been achieved. Delivering the Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at the University of Oxford on November 18, 2026, she emphasized that substantive equality requires addressing intersecting structural disadvantages like caste, class, and unpaid domestic labor. She noted that formal legislation alone cannot guarantee safety, education, or inheritance rights for all women.
articles.description: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

articles.headline: Haiti police say 34 gang members killed in capital raid
articles.title: Haiti police say 34 gang members killed in capital raid
articles.description: Haitian police say at least 34 gang members were killed in an operation in the capital city of Port-au-Prince.

articles.headline: Canada embraces artificial intelligence data centres as United States faces public pushback
articles.title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back
articles.summary: Canadian industry leaders and officials are positioning the country as a hub for artificial intelligence data centres as American communities increasingly reject local developments. Alberta has emerged as the centre of this boom, backed by abundant natural gas and government support for projects like Kevin O'Leary's Wonder Valley. However, rising local opposition, water usage concerns, and recent protests in Nova Scotia indicate that public resistance is beginning to surface across Canada.
articles.description: Shark Tank's Kevin O'Leary is among the big investors looking to Canada as a data centre development destination, while his US project faces local opposition.

articles.headline: Four bodies recovered after migrant boat capsizes off coast of Senegal
articles.title: Four bodies recovered after Senegal boat capsizes amid migration surge
articles.summary: Four bodies were recovered after a migrant boat carrying at least fifty people struck a rock and capsized near Yenne, Senegal, as search operations continue for survivors. According to Horizons Sans Frontieres President Boubacar Seye, the tragic incident coincides with a significant surge in Atlantic migration attempts toward Spain's Canary Islands, prompting growing concern from United Nations agencies and local authorities over rising fatalities along the dangerous maritime route.
articles.description: Search for survivors continues near Yenne as migrant arrivals in Spain's Canary Islands surge by nearly two-thirds.

articles.headline: Donald Trump grants posthumous presidential pardon to baseball player Pete Rose
articles.title: Trump posthumously pardons US baseball legend Pete Rose
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump issued a posthumous and symbolic presidential pardon to late baseball player Pete Rose on Thursday. Rose, who accumulated a record 4,256 career hits playing for Major League Baseball, pleaded guilty to tax evasion in 1990 and received a lifetime ban for gambling. Although reinstated last year, the pardon does not alter his Hall of Fame eligibility.
articles.description: Rose, who died in 2024, was given a lifetime ban from the sport for betting on games but was reinstated last year.

articles.headline: Natural gas explosion kills six people in Tbilisi apartment building
articles.title: Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Georgia apartment building
articles.summary: Six individuals died when a suspected natural gas explosion caused a partial collapse of a residential building in Tbilisi on Thursday morning. Emergency workers rescued a three-year-old girl and an eleven-year-old boy from the wreckage in the Ponichala district. Georgian authorities launched a criminal investigation into safety regulation violations, while the mayor announced temporary relocations for affected families.
articles.description: Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said rescuers had recovered six bodies from the wreckage.

articles.headline: Mahua Moitra accuses BJP supporters of attacking her convoy
articles.title: Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters
articles.summary: All India Trinamool Congress parliamentarian Mahua Moitra alleged that political opponents targeted her vehicle with stones and eggs in Nadia district. Writing on social media on November 19, 2026, the legislator claimed local law enforcement colluded with approximately ninety members of the opposing party to disrupt her scheduled programme. There was no immediate official response from police or accused groups regarding the incident.
articles.description: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

articles.headline: Clashes erupt at Medical College in Kolkata following principal gherao
articles.title: Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal government, Left student’s unions at loggerheads
articles.summary: Tensions escalated at the Medical College in Kolkata on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, after junior doctors gheraoed the principal and outsiders subsequently attacked protesting students and damaged property. The demonstration followed show-cause notices issued to eight junior doctors who protested during the Chorbagan stampede. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad denied involvement in the clashes, while Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee criticized the demonstrating medical personnel.
articles.description: Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee

articles.headline: Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma approaches three-year term
articles.title: Nearing 3 years as Rajasthan CM, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to assert his authority
articles.summary: Nearly three years after Bhajan Lal Sharma assumed office in December 2023 as Rajasthan Chief Minister, Congress State President Govind Singh Dotasara has shifted his criticism from labeling him a remote-controlled leader to accusing him of dismantling the Bharatiya Janata Party within the state. Mr. Sharma was initially selected as a first-time MLA by the central party leadership, drawing early skepticism from political opponents.
articles.description: Having entered office with virtually no administrative experience, his tenure has been a continuous tightrope walk between balancing the demands of the party’s central leadership and build authority of his own within the State.

articles.headline: Apple is hiring engineers to build an AI agent
articles.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
articles.summary: Apple is actively recruiting engineers to develop a new artificial intelligence assistant capable of executing multi-step tasks across web browsers, applications, and command lines. According to Bloomberg, the initiative involves collaboration between the Siri, user interface frameworks, and foundation models divisions. This development follows recent software updates that expand developer access to Siri integration.
articles.description: Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That's according to a now-removed job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which said Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI […]

articles.headline: Rajasthan High Court declines interim stay on corruption probe against IAS officer
articles.title: Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS officer corruption probe
articles.summary: The Rajasthan High Court refused an interim stay on Thursday regarding an investigation into senior Indian Administrative Service officer Shikhar Agarwal. The Anti-Corruption Bureau alleged Agarwal abused his position to provide undue benefits to a private firm in exchange for luxury villas. The court directed the state government to respond to the petition within three weeks.
articles.description: The ACB has alleged that IAS officer Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm

articles.headline: Nvidia experiences stock volatility amid former CEO departure
articles.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
articles.summary: Nvidia shares dropped significantly following the resignation of former chief executive Jensen Huang amid reports of personal misconduct and an independent board investigation. Interim chief executive Colette Kress reported strong financial results for the third quarter with total revenue reaching $115.8 billion. Meanwhile, the company announced that Huang will not be reinstated and is currently searching for a permanent replacement.
articles.description: "We've got this," Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company's third quarter earnings call. By Thursday, the company's stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings […]

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet orders confiscation of book accused of insulting Basavanna
articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet okays confiscation of book that ‘insults’ Basavanna and ‘distorts’ his philosophy
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet decided on Thursday to confiscate copies of the book Basava Mantapa by author Ravi Hanj following complaints that it distorts the philosophy of Basavanna. Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara announced that legal action will also be taken against publisher Vishveshwar Bhat, as the government seeks to address concerns raised by the Basava Samiti.
articles.description: Basava Samiti has accused U.S.-based author Ravi Hanj of hurting the sentiments of followers of the 12th century social reformer Basavanna in his book ‘Basava Mantapa’

articles.headline: Haitian police report thirty-four suspected gang members killed
articles.title: Haiti police say at least 34 suspected gang members killed in raid
articles.summary: Haitian national police announced that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed during a security operation in the Martissant neighbourhood of Port-au-Prince. Officers conducted the raid alongside an anti-gang task force including personnel from private security firm Vectus Global. The strategic neighbourhood has remained under gang control since 2021, severely disrupting local transport and commerce.
articles.description: Police say the raid targeted the Martissant area, located on a key route out of Port-au-Prince held by gangs since 2021.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice delivers landmark Rohingya judgment
articles.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice delivered a landmark judgment regarding the Rohingya community on November 19, 2026, returning the crisis to international attention. A former United Nations official reflected on decades of diplomatic challenges, highlighting that legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The situation remains deeply rooted in historical, political, and postcolonial disputes surrounding identity and citizenship.
articles.description: The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

articles.headline: West Bengal districts issue alerts for cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
articles.summary: Several districts in southern West Bengal, including Kolkata, issued heavy rainfall alerts as cyclonic storm Akvan approaches the coast. According to the India Meteorological Department, the storm was located over the east-central Bay of Bengal on November 19, 2026, and is expected to make landfall between Narsipatnam and Puri. Authorities have cancelled 19 train services and advised fishermen to avoid deep sea areas.
articles.description: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD

articles.headline: Jasprit Bumrah receives widespread acclaim from pundits and peers for exceptional bowling performances.
articles.title: Bumrah — the postman who seldom fails to deliver
articles.summary: India national cricket team fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah has earned global recognition for his exceptional accuracy and skill on the field. Analysts and senior athletes frequently praise his unique bowling action and consistent wicket-taking ability. Discovered by former India coach John Wright, the athlete now requires careful workload management by the national board to preserve his physical condition for major international tournaments.
articles.description: Plucked out from anonymity despite an action that could so easily have put the traditionalists off, he took little time to establish himself as a premier paceman; his unique skill-sets allowed him to flourish anywhere in the world, on any kind of track because he can take the pitch out of the equation effortlessly

articles.headline: Ten killed in Pakistan as bus crashes into gas tanker
articles.title: Ten killed in Pakistan as bus crashes into gas tanker
articles.description: Ten people were killed and at least 27 more injured after a passenger bus collided with an LPG tanker in Pakistan.

articles.headline: Rohingya genocide survivor: ‘perpetrators will have to face consequences’
articles.title: Rohingya genocide survivor: ‘perpetrators will have to face consequences’
articles.description: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.

articles.headline: Salvadoran troops expand military operations against armed gangs in Haiti
articles.title: Why are Bukele’s Salvadoran troops in Haiti and what have they achieved?
articles.summary: President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador has deployed approximately 2,500 soldiers to Port-au-Prince following the October kidnapping of four aviation technicians. The military presence has grown into a major offensive alongside local forces to combat armed groups controlling the capital. While desperate residents praise the intervention for addressing severe security crises, monitors report rising casualties and warn of potential risks to civilians.
articles.description: With crowds rallying behind El Salvador's deployment in Haiti, analysts question whether civilians are any safer.

articles.headline: West Bengal police file FIR against two former state ministers
articles.title: FIR against two former Bengal Ministers over sexual assault charges
articles.summary: Authorities lodged a First Information Report at Baguiati Police Station against former ministers Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu. Social activist Rajib Sarkar filed the case on behalf of department employees alleging sexual assault, rape, and corruption. The accused previously served in the Trinamool Congress government led by then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.
articles.description: Five former Ministers, who had been part of Mamata Banerjee’s cabinet, have been arrested since the BJP government came to power in May 2026

articles.headline: How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US
articles.title: How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US
articles.description: Measles is making a comeback in the US as vaccination rates fall.

articles.headline: US judge allows defamation lawsuit by Trump against media companies
articles.title: Trump’s case against NYT and Penguin Random House may proceed: Judge
articles.summary: United States District Judge Steven Merryday ruled that a defamation lawsuit filed by President Donald Trump against The New York Times and Penguin Random House may proceed. The legal action targets articles and a book concerning Trump's business background and 2024 election campaign. Defendants denied the allegations, arguing the case lacks legal merit.
articles.description: The lawsuit cited a book about Trump by two NYT reporters and what it said were 'false, malicious, defamatory' articles.

articles.headline: Google updates homepage with new collapsible AI chat sidebar
articles.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
articles.summary: Google is updating its desktop homepage globally to include a collapsible sidebar for AI searches. According to Robby Stein, vice president of product, users can click a gray bar on the left side of the screen to view recent AI Mode searches, start new threads, search existing threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook to help manage complex and multi-step queries.
articles.description: Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google's vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats. Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the […]

articles.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth meets Colombian leaders in Bogota
articles.title: ‘On the same page’: Hegseth hails US ties with Colombia’s de la Espriella
articles.summary: United States Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth visited Bogota on Wednesday to meet with Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Mora and discuss regional cooperation against organized crime. During the visit, officials announced Colombia as the likely host for next year's Americas Counter Cartel Coalition meeting and formalised the delivery of a Lockheed C-130 Hercules plane, despite reports of disagreements regarding direct US military intervention.
articles.description: The US defence secretary praised security cooperation with Colombia as country joins Americas Counter Cartel Coalition.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI launch highlights cultural dominance amid industry struggles
articles.title: Blockbuster GTA VI release shows cultural, economic heft of video games
articles.summary: Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI, generating over $1.5 billion in pre-sales and earning critical acclaim for its depiction of Vice City. The launch underscores the economic heft of the United States entertainment sector, even as developers face mass layoffs and studio closures across the country. According to industry data, 40 studios closed in 2026.
articles.description: Runaway success of popular franchise comes as video game industry has struggled with mass layoffs in recent years.

articles.headline: Eelam Tamil poet and academic Rudhramoorthy Cheran dies at 68
articles.title: Cheran, the poet who chronicled Eelam’s war and memory, passes away at 68
articles.summary: Rudhramoorthy Cheran, an Eelam Tamil poet, essayist, and professor of sociology and criminology at the University of Windsor, passed away in Canada at the age of 68. Hailing from Jaffna, he emerged as a leading voice of wartime literature and diasporic experiences, chronicling decades of Tamil life. His celebrated works have been translated into multiple languages, and he is survived by his wife and two children.
articles.description: Hailing from Alaveddy in Jaffna, Cheran was a multifaceted artist — a poet, short story writer, essayist, and painter. Alongside his poetry, he frequently contributed essays in both Tamil and English to various journals.

articles.headline: French court prepares to deliver verdict in police beating trial
articles.title: France awaits verdict six years after police beat Black music producer
articles.summary: A Paris court is expected to deliver its verdict regarding three French police officers accused of assaulting Black music producer Michel Zecler twenty-nine times in November 2020. Prosecutors have requested prison sentences and professional bans for Aurelien Lapersonne, Pierre Plantier, and Philippe Tondeux, who allegedly also falsified reports. The high-profile case has intensified national debates surrounding institutional racism, police brutality, and proposed self-defence legislation.
articles.description: Three officers are accused of assaulting Michel Zecler in an incident that was filmed by surveillance cameras.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit hands over ten patented technologies
articles.title: 10 patented technologies handed over to various firms at T.N. Tech Transfer Summit
articles.summary: Ten patented innovations developed in higher education institutions were handed over to start-up firms and micro, enterprises during the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit. Co-organized by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology and Anna University, the event featured a coffee cherry harvesting toolkit created by school students. Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan inaugurated the summit, which featured memoranda of understanding signed with institutions including IIT-Madras.
articles.description: Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, says it will be made into an annual affair and will be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well

articles.headline: Dr. NTRUHS plans new programs and research network for medical colleges
articles.title: Dr. NTRUHS plans AI-based courses in affiliated colleges to strengthen research collaboration
articles.summary: Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences is planning to introduce artificial intelligence and machine learning academic programs while establishing a university-wide Research and Innovation Network. These initiatives were discussed during a meeting of affiliated college principals and research members led by Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar. Additionally, plans for the Amaravati School of Bio-Design aim to unite medical professionals and engineers to address healthcare challenges starting in December 2026.
articles.description: The university examining the feasibility of introducing interdisciplinary certificate and diploma programmes in emerging areas of health sciences

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu plans central digital repository for institutional research
articles.title: Repository to catalogue research occurring at institutions in T.N. to be set up, says Higher Education Secretary
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department will establish a central digital portal to catalogue research and innovation across state institutions, as announced by Higher Education Secretary Dheeraj Kumar. Anna University has been tasked with leading the development of the platform, which will connect universities, industry stakeholders, and governmental organizations to streamline technology transfer and commercialization efforts throughout the state.
articles.description: He announces that Anna University has been asked to take the lead in developing this digital platform

articles.headline: Telangana chief minister launches Indiramma family insurance scheme in Siddipet
articles.title: CM launches Indiramma family life insurance scheme
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the Indiramma Family Insurance scheme in Siddipet on November 20, 2026, offering five lakh rupees in insurance cover to every state family. Addressing a public meeting, Mr. Reddy criticized BRS leaders K. Chandrasekhar Rao and T. Harish Rao over governance and water sharing, while highlighting upcoming welfare measures like free sarees and housing.
articles.description: Siddipet Govt medical college to be named after late Congress stalwart Madan Mohan

articles.headline: Congress reshuffles organization by relieving twenty-five AICC secretaries
articles.title: Congress relieves 25 AICC secretaries of responsibilities in organisational reshuffle
articles.summary: The Congress party carried out an organizational reshuffle on November 19, 2026, relieving twenty-five All India Congress Committee secretaries and joint secretaries of their duties. Approved by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and announced by general secretary K.C. Venugopal, the changes assign fresh charges to eighty-one office-bearers across multiple states, union territories, and departments.
articles.description: The party assigns fresh charges to 81 office-bearers across States, Union Territories and organisational departments

articles.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan demands judicial probe into Keralam power purchase deals
articles.title: Keralam CM’s claims incorrect, judicial probe needed into power purchase deals, says Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan criticized Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on November 19, 2026, demanding a judicial inquiry into contentious power purchase agreements. Mr. Vijayan alleged that a deal with VEH Global India Pvt Ltd involved intended corruption worth two hundred fifty-two crore rupees, arguing the state faced no power shortages during that period.
articles.description: Pinarayi says that Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s justification that electricity was procured from VEH Global via a bilateral arrangement as there were no takers for tenders floated by the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) was incorrect

articles.headline: Iraq reaches compromise with Kataib Hezbollah over Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold
articles.title: Iraq reaches compromise with Kataib Hezbollah over armed group’s stronghold
articles.summary: Iraq announced a compromise with the Iranian-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah to establish a joint operations centre in the strategic town of Jurf al-Sakhar. Revealed on November 20, 2026, the agreement follows recent tensions over oil smuggling allegations and deploys a combined security force consisting of the army, federal police, energy police, and Popular Mobilisation Forces.
articles.description: The compromise reached will unite forces that include brigades from the Popular Mobilisation Forces.

articles.headline: Karnataka cabinet approves infrastructure projects and state highway developments
articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears projects worth ₹4,000 crore for Bengaluru city, approves ₹10,250 crore for development of nine State Highways
articles.summary: The Karnataka government on November 19, 2026, cleared over four thousand crore rupees for Bengaluru city projects and approved ten thousand two hundred fifty crore rupees to develop nine state highways. Officials also advanced electric bus deployments, road white-topping, minority student laptop distributions, and legislative bills during the cabinet meeting.

articles.headline: Karnataka health department launches antimicrobial resistance containment plan
articles.title: Karnataka launches State action plan for containment of antimicrobial resistance
articles.summary: The Department of Health and Family Welfare launched the Karnataka State Action Plan for Containment of Antimicrobial Resistance on November 19, 2026, in Bengaluru. Officials stated the initiative aims to strengthen antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance, and multi-sectoral collaboration to address growing public health threats across the state.

articles.headline: Pakistani security forces kill twenty two militants in northwest raids
articles.title: Pakistan military says it killed 22 militants in raids on hideouts
articles.summary: Pakistani security forces killed twenty two militants during intelligence-based operations in the South Waziristan, Bannu, and Tank districts over forty eight hours, the military announced on November 19, 2026. Officials alleged the slain fighters received backing from India, while leaders praised the security personnel for countering rising militant violence in the region.
articles.description: Pakistan’s military says security forces have raided militant hideouts in the northwest near the Afghan border, setting off gunbattles that killed 22 militants

articles.headline: Regulators stress need for deeper capital markets to fund India growth
articles.title: SEBI, PFRDA call for deeper capital markets to fund Viksit Bharat 2047
articles.summary: India requires deeper capital markets and stronger domestic savings mobilisation to finance the Viksit Bharat 2047 goals, according to Securities and Exchange Board of India whole-time member K.V.R. Murty. Speaking at a Mumbai summit on November 19, 2026, officials highlighted that traditional bank lending alone remains insufficient for major infrastructure and long-term project requirements.
articles.description: Sustained participation by retail investors and domestic institutional investors (DIIs) had helped Indian markets remain resilient amid volatility caused by foreign portfolio investor outflows over the past year.

articles.headline: Susan Smith denied parole thirty two years after drowning her sons
articles.title: Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
articles.summary: Susan Smith, fifty five, was unanimously denied parole by a seven-member South Carolina board on November 19, 2026, following her 1994 conviction for drowning her two young sons. The children's father opposed her release during the hearing, while Smith expressed remorse and stated she has matured during thirty two years of incarceration.
articles.description: At a hearing on the possibility of parole, Smith said she wished she could change the past, and her two children "did not deserve to die".

articles.headline: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Vladimir Putin agree to maintain communication
articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to keep talking following their meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. Ms. Takaichi urged the release of a detained journalist and raised concerns over the treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia amid long-standing territorial disputes.
articles.description: The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

articles.headline: India opt to field first against New Zealand in opening Test
articles.title: IND vs NZ, 1st Test: Nicholls, Phillips revive New Zealand after early hiccups
articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss on Wednesday at the Basin Reserve, choosing to bowl first in the opening Test against New Zealand. India made several changes to their lineup, leaving out Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja while selecting four pace bowlers. New Zealand kept the same eleven players they announced earlier in the week.
articles.description: The softer ball and clear skies made conditions easier to bat, but Nicholls and Phillips pounced on virtually every scoring opportunity. Their partnership not only arrested the slide but also ensured India’s four-pronged pace attack had little to show for its toil after lunch

articles.headline: New genetic study reveals Rohingya share genomic ancestry with Bangladeshis and Burmese
articles.title: Rohingya a ‘distinct lineage’ close to Bangladeshis and Burmese: Study
articles.summary: A genomic study published in Scientific Reports indicates the Rohingya are a distinct ethnic group with ancestry closely linked to Bangladeshis and considerable mixture from Burmese lineages. The findings emerge alongside an International Court of Justice ruling that found Myanmar committed genocide against the Muslim minority population located in north Rakhine State.
articles.description: The International Court of Justice held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State

articles.headline: Taiz faces water shortages and public health risks amid Houthi siege
articles.title: Yemen’s besieged city of Taiz faces a deepening water crisis
articles.summary: Water production in Taiz has nearly halved following a siege imposed by the Houthi group in October, leaving over 800,000 residents cut off from aid. According to local officials, commercial prices have surged while emergency wells suffer from contamination due to uncollected waste, prompting hospital administrators to warn of a potential public health disaster in Yemen.
articles.description: Fuel shortages and the loss of access to wells have left residents dependent on unsafe water.

articles.headline: Francisco Javier Vera Manzanares discusses child climate activism and rights
articles.title: Children are political agents whose active participation strengthens democracy, says International Children’s Peace Prize winner Francisco Javier
articles.summary: Seventeen-year-old Colombian climate activist and International Children’s Peace Prize winner Francisco Javier Vera Manzanares emphasized that children function as political agents capable of strengthening democracy. Having relocated to Spain following security threats in Colombia, he continues his environmental advocacy through the Guardians for Life movement, addressing challenges including climate finance limitations and the environmental impact of artificial intelligence data centres.
articles.description: As the 22nd winner of the International Children’s Peace Prize, Francisco has joined a distinguished list of past laureates that includes Malala Yousafzai and Greta Thunberg

articles.headline: India's crude oil imports from OPEC countries decline to 27.4 percent
articles.title: OPEC share in India’s crude imports drops to 27.4% in Apr-Oct amid West Asia flare-ups
articles.summary: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries' share in India's crude oil imports fell to 27.4% between April and October, down from 38.5% during the same period last year. According to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell, India increased total imports by 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes while diversifying its procurement sources amid regional conflicts.
articles.description: During the mentioned period, India’s crude oil imports spurred about 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT)

articles.headline: Government revises PUC certificate validity rules for BS-VI vehicles
articles.title: Centre extends pollution certificate validity to up to three years for newer vehicles
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways notified amended rules on November 13 altering Pollution Under Control certificate renewal intervals. Under the new schedule, BS-VI private vehicles under six years old require renewal every three years, while older vehicles face stricter timelines. Compliance periods vary from six months to three years depending on vehicle age and emission standards to streamline testing.
articles.description: As per the changes, owners of newer vehicles will be required to renew their pollution certificates less frequently, while older vehicles will continue to undergo more regular emission testing. The move is aimed at aligning the frequency of emission testing with the age profile of vehicles

articles.headline: Indian stock markets rebound over 1% as banking and auto sectors drive gains
articles.title: Sensex, Nifty surge over 1% as banks, auto stocks drive rally; Bank Nifty hits record high
articles.summary: Indian equity markets recovered strongly on Thursday following three sessions of muted trading, with the Sensex rising 929.05 points and the Nifty 50 gaining 286.35 points. According to Bajaj Broking deputy vice-president Pabitro Mukherjee, foreign portfolio investor inflows and lower commodity prices supported the rally, which pushed the Bank Nifty index to a record high of 63,063.
articles.description: “Going ahead we expect the index to extend the up move and head towards 63,500-63,800 levels in the coming sessions being the measuring implication of the recent range breakout of 58,700-54,000,” Mr. Mukherjee said.

articles.headline: Dozens of migrants missing after wooden boat capsizes off Senegal
articles.title: Dozens missing after boat carrying migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
articles.summary: Senegalese authorities extended rescue operations following the capsizing of a wooden pirogue carrying approximately 100 migrants near the coastal village of Yenne. Local media outlets reported that at least four bodies were recovered from the wreckage, while numerous individuals remained unaccounted for. President Diomaye Faye ordered the interior ministry to investigate the rising number of irregular maritime departures toward Europe following the disaster.
articles.description: At least four bodies have been recovered from the boat which was reportedly carrying between 50 and 100 people.

articles.headline: India defeats Malaysia 4-1 in Women's Asian Champions Trophy opening match
articles.title: Women’s Asian Champions Trophy: India women assert dominance after initial setback
articles.summary: India secured a 4-1 victory against Malaysia at the Women's Asian Champions Trophy on November 19, 2026, overcoming an early deficit at the International Sports Complex. Trailing after a goal from Nuramirah Zulkifli, Sjoerd Marijne's squad responded through Mumtaz Khan, Salima Tete, Puja Sahoo, and Lalremsiami to successfully launch their title defence in front of home supporters.
articles.description: The defending champion makes good of multiple penalty corners to overpower Malaysia after conceding an early goal; China thrashes Thailand; Japan edges South Korea

articles.headline: OpenAI introduces live dictation feature for ChatGPT across all platforms
articles.title: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched a live dictation feature for ChatGPT that transcribes audio prompts in real time as users speak. Available globally on web, desktop, and mobile apps, the update also removes the previous 10-minute recording limit for voice dictation. Users can view and edit generated transcripts directly within the prompt box to improve overall input efficiency.
articles.description: ChatGPT can receive audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It's rolling out now globally on all ChatGPT plans on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android apps. While using dictation in ChatGPT, you can tap or […]

articles.headline: Putin pitches Arctic shipping route investments during Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit
articles.title: Putin pitches Arctic route, calls for investment: Will it work?
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin used his address at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday to encourage foreign investment in the Northern Sea Route, proposing financial incentives such as tax breaks. While Moscow aims to establish year-round navigation, analysts caution that harsh conditions, environmental risks, and geopolitical concerns remain significant obstacles to commercial viability.
articles.description: Analysts say some Asian investors may show interest, but the route is unlikely to be a viable global shipping lane.

articles.headline: Minister Gadkari urges engineers to prioritize road safety and biofuels
articles.title: Union Minister Gadkari calls for alternative fuel use, raises grave concerns over road safety
articles.summary: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari addressed the 85th Indian Roads Congress on Thursday, demanding greater accountability from engineers regarding accident-prone black spots. He criticized current project reporting practices and advocated for the adoption of biofuels to reduce fossil fuel imports, noting that such a shift could significantly benefit rural agricultural communities.

articles.headline: Bajaj Integrated Health System plans 2,500 crore rupee healthcare network investment
articles.title: Bajaj Group-backed BIHS to invest ₹2,500 cr. in healthcare venture Nivara, target 10-plus cities
articles.summary: Bajaj Integrated Health System will invest approximately 2,500 crore rupees to establish Nivara, an integrated healthcare network starting in Pune before expanding to over ten cities within fifteen years. Led by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Nirav Bajaj, the initiative will launch medical centres, ambulatory facilities, and hospitals to deliver continuous health management across India.
articles.description: Nivara will be rolled out across three formats — Medical Centres, Ambulatory Centres and Hospitals — over the next few years.

articles.headline: Family to appeal verdict in Ariyil Shukkoor murder case
articles.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder case: victim’s family, IUML leadership to continue legal battle as convicts seek leniency
articles.summary: The family of slain Indian Union Muslim League activist Ariyil Shukkoor plans to challenge a Special CBI Court verdict that acquitted 18 individuals, including two prominent political leaders. Meanwhile, 13 convicted persons have requested sentencing leniency, citing family responsibilities, health issues, and their status as sole breadwinners while asking to be imprisoned in Kannur jail.
articles.description: League’s Kannur unit describes the verdict, which acquitted 18 accused, as ‘disappointing and unexpected.’ Those convicted plead for leniency stating that they are the sole breadwinners of their families

articles.headline: Jagan Mohan Reddy supports demands for comprehensive caste census
articles.title: Jagan bats for a caste census that ensures inclusive, equitable growth
articles.summary: YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy met with the All India Caste Census Coordination Committee on Thursday to discuss the upcoming 2027 Census. He endorsed calls for a mandatory caste column and detailed economic indicators, arguing that empirical data is essential for effective policy-making and ensuring equitable growth for all social groups.
articles.description: An accurate and comprehensive census is essential for evidence-based policy-making and effective implementation of welfare and development programmes, says the YSRCP president

articles.headline: New national guidelines released for wastewater pathogen surveillance
articles.title: CSIR-CCMB-led effort shapes national wastewater surveillance guidelines to monitor diverse pathogens
articles.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has released national guidelines for monitoring pathogens in wastewater, a project shaped by the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology. The initiative aims to detect viruses and bacteria early to support public health. This effort builds on surveillance protocols developed during the COVID-19 pandemic to strengthen national disease monitoring.

articles.headline: Indian food inflation reaches 8.9% with significant price increases across essential commodities.
articles.title: The average cost of a thali has jumped by 16% in less than 10 months
articles.summary: Food inflation across India reached 8.9% last month, marking the highest rate recorded in twenty-two months according to official data. Retail prices for essential commodities surged between January and October, led by onions increasing by more than 100% since March. Garlic prices rose by 22% and rice increased by 11%, contributing to a 16% jump in the average cost of a meal.
articles.description: Food inflation has raised meal costs, forcing households to spend a larger share of their wages on food

articles.headline: Bharat Rashtra Samithi leader K.T. Rama Rao accuses Congress government of corruption
articles.title: KTR accuses Congress govt. of corruption, alleges irregularities in public spending
articles.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. Rama Rao accused the ruling Congress administration of severe financial irregularities and mismanagement on November 19, 2026. Speaking at Telangana Bhavan, he cited allegations by Congress legislators regarding commission demands and tender corruption. Furthermore, he claimed the government reduced pension beneficiary numbers by approximately 7,000, impacting vulnerable citizens across Telangana significantly.

articles.headline: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan promises data-driven governance and administrative efficiency
articles.title: CM promises a data-driven and efficient governance; Medisep to be restructured
articles.summary: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan announced the implementation of an artificial intelligence-powered file management system to enhance administrative efficiency on November 19, 2026. Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram at the Kerala Secretariat Association anniversary, he pledged to restructure the Medical Insurance Scheme for State Employees and Pensioners while highlighting a 28 percent growth in state Goods and Services Tax revenue.
articles.description: He pledges phased restoration of benefits for government employees, including potential pay revisions, along with continued and targeted fiscal measures to sustain growth and new investments.

articles.headline: CBT approves systematic withdrawal plan for retiring EPF members
articles.title: EPFO relaxes withdrawal norms; lowers minimum balance requirement to 10%
articles.summary: The Central Board of Trustees approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan enabling retiring Employees' Provident Fund Organisation members to receive accumulated savings in periodic instalments rather than a lump sum. EPFO sources stated the initiative enhances financial security and allows nominees to withdraw remaining balances in the event of a member's death during the payout period.
articles.description: SWP will enable members to convert their savings into a predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving ownership of the underlying corpus, says the Labour Ministry

articles.headline: Venture capital firms commit 1,050 crore rupees in DeepTech during Bengaluru Tech Summit
articles.title: 24 VCs make investment commitments for ₹1,050 crore in DeepTech at BTS 2026
articles.summary: Twenty-four venture capital firms pledged approximately 1,050 crore rupees toward DeepTech initiatives during the Future Makers Conclave at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on November 19, 2026. IT and BT Minister Priyank Kharge highlighted the milestone alongside a decade of achievements from the ELEVATE program, which has supported 1,084 start-ups across Karnataka to expand regional innovation ecosystems.
articles.description: This marks a significant leap from the 2025 edition, where the Government of Karnataka and venture capitalists disbursed ₹400 crore towards AI and DeepTech startups, say industry observers

articles.headline: FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 begins in Qatar following United States withdrawal
articles.title: FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 gets under way in Qatar despite USA withdrawal
articles.summary: The FIFA Under-17 World Cup commenced in Qatar on Thursday, featuring forty-eight teams competing across twenty-four days at the Aspire Zone complex in Doha. The global tournament proceeded despite the United States national team withdrawing over security concerns last week, a decision dismissed by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who stated that participants remain safe in the host nation.
articles.description: The 25-day tournament will feature 48 teams, with Dominican Republic replacing USA as FIFA plays down security concerns.

articles.headline: Malaysia to end visa-free entry for Indian nationals in 2027
articles.title: Malaysia to end visa-free entry to Indians from January 1, 2027
articles.summary: The Immigration Department of Malaysia announced that visa-free access for Indian nationals will end on January 1, 2027, replacing the current 30-day exemption introduced in December 2023. Visitors arriving after this date must obtain a visa via the MyVISA portal starting December 1, 2026. The High Commission of India previously warned travellers against misusing the tourist facility for employment.
articles.description: Earlier, Indian nationals travelling to the South East Asian nation were granted a 30-day visa exemption and just had to register for Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival

articles.headline: South Korean Supreme Court orders retrial for former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo
articles.title: South Korean court orders retrial for ex-PM Han over martial law attempt
articles.summary: South Korea's Supreme Court overturned the fifteen-year prison sentence of seventy-seven-year-old former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, ordering a lower court retrial regarding his actions during a brief martial law declaration two years ago. The ruling concluded that justices found shortcomings in assessing whether Han intended to undermine the Constitution, following the 2024 decree by former President Yoon Suk Yeol.
articles.description: The lower Seoul High Court will now retry the case based on the Supreme Court's legal interpretation of insurrection.

articles.headline: Dutch church hosts continuous service to shield asylum-seeking Babayants family
articles.title: Two years in, Dutch church’s nonstop service shields family seeking asylum
articles.summary: The Open Hof Protestant church in Kampen, Netherlands, has maintained a nonstop religious service for over seven hundred days to protect the Babayants family from deportation to Uzbekistan. Led by pastor Kasper Jager and supported by thousands of volunteers, the sanctuary utilises a Dutch legal provision preventing authorities from interrupting services, highlighting ongoing debates over children's rights and immigration policy.
articles.description: Under Dutch law, police cannot enter a church as long as a religious service is taking place.

articles.headline: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence seizes over 70 kg of heroin in Chennai
articles.title: DRI seizes over 70 kg of heroin worth ₹700 crore in Chennai
articles.summary: Revenue intelligence officials seized more than 70 kilograms of heroin valued at approximately 700 crore rupees during a raid at an ice manufacturing facility in Madhavaram. Two Tamil Nadu natives identified as Abdul Shukoor and Shafiq Ahmed were arrested and subsequently remanded to judicial custody by an Alandur court.
articles.description: DRI officials raided an ice-manufacturing factory in Madhavaram; DMK president M.K. Stalin says Tamil Nadu has become a ‘vice city’ under TVK rule

articles.headline: US consortium Frontier Minerals wins tender for Kenya mining project
articles.title: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
articles.summary: Frontier Minerals, a US-led consortium comprising three American companies, secured the tender to develop Kenya's Mrima Hill mining project in Kwale County, surpassing seven international bidders. The site contains critical mineral deposits valued above sixty billion dollars, with the proposal aiming to establish domestic processing capacity while addressing environmental and community concerns raised by local residents.
articles.description: The Mrima Hill site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn).

articles.headline: Indian equity indices rebound as Sensex surges nearly 1,000 points
articles.title: Markets bounce back led by auto, bank stocks; Sensex surges nearly 1,000 pts, Nifty reclaims 25,500
articles.summary: Indian benchmark equity indices rebounded strongly on November 19, 2026, driven by gains in automobile and banking stocks alongside foreign fund inflows and easing commodity prices. The Bombay Stock Exchange Sensex climbed 989.94 points to close at 83,021.75, while the National Stock Exchange Nifty settled above 25,500. Foreign Institutional Investors purchased equities worth ₹5,866.78 crore in the preceding session.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 989.94 points, or 1.21%, to close at 83,021.75; During the day, it surged 1,012.06 points, or 1.23%, to 83,043.87

articles.headline: Can Anthropic afford to put AI safety first?
articles.title: Can Anthropic afford to put AI safety first?
articles.description: As Anthropic goes public, can the AI company balance its safety promises with the pressure to keep investors happy?

articles.headline: Russian military officer spotted carrying nuclear briefcase at APEC summit
articles.title: What is a ‘nuclear briefcase’, spotted at the APEC summit?
articles.summary: During trilateral talks in Shenzhen on Thursday, a Russian naval officer accompanying President Vladimir Putin was identified carrying the Cheget nuclear briefcase, which provides direct access to the nation's command network. Similar to the US nuclear football, the device serves as a symbolic reminder of Russia's nuclear arsenal and allows leaders to authorize strikes from any location globally.
articles.description: Vladimir Putin's special briefcase - thought to carry access to nuclear weapons - made a rare appearance in Shenzhen.

articles.headline: National Medical Commission asks colleges to join PM-RAHAT scheme
articles.title: NMC asks government medical colleges to onboard PM-RAHAT scheme for cashless emergency care
articles.summary: The National Medical Commission instructed government medical colleges and attached hospitals to adopt the Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment scheme to offer cashless emergency care. Launched on February 13, 2026, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the program provides up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for seven days. Facilities can register under different categories following National Health Authority guidelines overseen by state authorities.
articles.description: PM-RAHAT provides cashless treatment of up to ₹1.5 lakh per road accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals

articles.headline: Union Health Ministry proposes including antimicrobials in new drug definition
articles.title: Health Ministry proposes to include antimicrobials in ‘New Drug’ definition, separate licence for bulk drug wholesale
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry proposed amending the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules to classify antimicrobials as new drugs to address antimicrobial resistance and inadequate regulatory scrutiny. Additionally, the Ministry proposed separate licensing provisions under the Drugs Rules to establish dedicated wholesale oversight for bulk active and inactive substances across the pharmaceutical supply chain.
articles.description: Draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, and the Drugs Rules, 1945, would require manufacturers of antimicrobials to obtain Central Licensing Authority permission before applying for a State licence, amid concerns over antimicrobial resistance, and introduce separate forms for the wholesale sale of bulk drugs

articles.headline: Pew report predicts Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035
articles.title: Pew report predicts Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035
articles.description: A new Pew Research Center report projects that Islam could become the world’s largest religion by 2035, driven primarily by demographic trends and higher fertility rates rather than religious conversion.

articles.headline: Florida pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon convicted over Haitian president assassination
articles.title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
articles.summary: Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a sixty-seven-year-old dual US-Haitian national and Florida pastor, was convicted on Wednesday in a federal court in Miami of eight charges, including conspiracy related to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. Prosecutors stated Sanon initially plotted to oust Moïse to secure government contracts, contributing to a political vacuum and severe gang violence in the Caribbean nation.
articles.description: Christian Emmanuel Sanon is convicted of involvement in the plot that resulted in the killing of Jovenel Moïse.

articles.headline: Government urges Supreme Court to reconsider nationwide private universities inquiry
articles.title: Government questions previous Supreme Court orders on nationwide enquiry into private universities
articles.summary: The Union government urged the Supreme Court on November 19, 2026, to restrict a student grievance case to individual relief rather than pursuing a nationwide inquiry into private universities. Additional Solicitor General K.M. Natraj told a Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath that previous orders forced states to file massive reports. The case originated from a 2025 petition by student Ayesh Jain against Amity University over harassment allegations.
articles.description: The Justice Amanullah Bench had sought a full disclosure of benefits granted by the Centre and States, including the terms of allotment of land and preferential treatment, on these private institutions
